h2: NDT training near Jacksonville: FSCJ courses, local inspection employers and online study compared
html:
NDT training near Jacksonville: FSCJ courses, local inspection employers and online study compared

Jacksonville stands out among Florida cities for NDT. It has college credit courses in individual NDT methods and several inspection employers that hire and train locally, alongside the naval aviation and ship repair work the city is known for. That gives someone searching "NDT training near me" here real choices. The comparison below covers what each one provides and where it stops.

Who offers NDT training around Jacksonville?

  • Florida State College at Jacksonville (FSCJ). The college catalog lists a three-credit Intro to Non-Destructive Testing (ETI 1121) covering visual, penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic, eddy current and thermography methods along with qualification and documentation standards. Method courses follow, including Magnetic Particle NDT (ETI 2124C), Eddy Current NDT (ETI 2125C) and Infrared Thermography NDT (ETI 2127C). These are credit courses at the Associate in Science level. Check which run each term, and ask for a record of hours and lab work that an employer's Level III can match against SNT-TC-1A.
  • Inspection labs hiring locally. A Mistras Group posting for a Level II technician in magnetic particle, penetrant and ultrasonic thickness testing at its Jacksonville lab accepted three backgrounds: graduation from an NDT technical program meeting SNT-TC-1A for those methods, a prior Level II with a year of experience, or Level I with enough field hours to certify to Level II. It also asked for proof of classroom hours and wanted local applicants.
  • Field roles with further training. In June 2026 Applied Technical Services advertised Level II UT shear wave openings assigned to its Jacksonville office and supporting customers statewide. The company said it would provide formal PAUT training and chances to build experience hours, and it asked for a drug screen, a clean driving record, US person status and willingness to travel.
  • Naval aviation and ship repair. Contractors on Navy work certify their people under SNT-TC-1A written practices and add the naval procedure requirements on top, so a solid civilian Level II is the entry ticket.

Which Jacksonville route fits you?

ProfileRoutePoint to remember
School leaver who wants a college recordFSCJ method courses, then a trainee jobCourses supply training hours; experience hours come only from supervised work
Working technician chasing a Level II posting like those aboveA method course plus documented field hoursPostings ask for proof of classroom hours, so keep the course record
UT technician heading for PAUTUT Level II, then employer PAUT trainingPhased array builds on conventional UT, not the other way round
Employer certifying a crewTraining at your facility, with Level III examsA written practice that matches the methods your contracts name

Questions to ask any NDT training provider near Jacksonville

  1. Will I leave with a record that shows topics and hours for each method, in the form local employers ask for?
  2. Are those hours enough for the SNT-TC-1A level I want? The hours planner shows the recommended figures by method.
  3. Who runs the hands-on part, and on what equipment and specimens?
  4. Who will actually certify me? A course or college cannot; your employer certifies under its written practice, or ASNT through its central exams.
  5. Is there a Level III I can put questions to while I train?

Where Atlantis fits for Jacksonville candidates and employers

Atlantis NDT keeps no classroom in Jacksonville; it is an online and on-site provider. Theory is self-paced on the Atlantis portal from the day you enroll, all year round, with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions. You practise technique in the Practical NDT simulator and complete the hands-on practical and the practical exam at your employer's facility under its written practice built on SNT-TC-1A. The methods Jacksonville postings ask for most map to ultrasonic, magnetic particle and penetrant training, at Level 2 for technicians who already hold Level I.

An FSCJ student can use our theory to fill a method the college is not running that term, and a lab technician can use it to add a level without leaving shift work. Employers along the St. Johns River can have training delivered at their own site with exams set by a Level III. Welding staff can compare AWS CWI exam prep in Jacksonville, and candidates near the Georgia line can also read NDT training in Savannah.
